newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng extends losses on currency woes.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng extends losses on currency woes.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index extended its losses on Tuesday, tumbling 621 points, or 3.86 percent, to 15,475 by late-morning as concerns about the stability of the Hong Kong dollar continued to pressure prices.
The Hong Kong dollar weakened during the morning against the U.S. dollar, trading at around HK$7.7427/37 compared with HK$7.7400 earlier in the day.
Overnight interest rates surged on Tuesday morning compared with Friday's levels but stabilised by late morning at around 9.50 to 10.00 percent.

"I think the speculation is unlikley to last longer, but I think it is reasonable to expect that there will be upward pressure on local interest rates going forward and that will definitely affect equity prices," said Benjamin Cheng, executive director at Goldman Sachs.
Interest-rate sensitive banking and property stocks were hit hard. Brokers said investors feared the rise in interbank rates would squeeze banks' profit margins and lead to higher mortgage rates.
Shares in HSBC Holdings fell to HK$262.00 compared with a close of HK$272.00 on Friday. Hang Seng Bank was off HK$3.00 at HK$101.50.

In the property sector, Cheung Kong tumbled HK$3.25 to HK$88.75, Henderson Land fell HK$2.75 to HK$67.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties was down HK$2.25 at HK$94.00. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
